title: OKF v0.2 Note Frontmatter
description: Validation contract for the YAML frontmatter block of a Note in a burlmd Workspace, expressed against the YAML block's decoded mapping. IMPORTANT: only `type` is conformance-bearing. Open Knowledge Format v0.2 section 11 makes a bundle conformant if every non-reserved .md file has a parseable frontmatter block containing a non-empty `type`, and it requires consumers to NOT reject a bundle for missing optional fields, unknown types, unknown keys, broken links, or missing indices. Every other property below is ADVISORY: it documents the shape burlmd recognises so it can surface those fields, and a value that does not match it MUST NOT set `okf_conformant = 0` -- doing so would flag legitimate foreign bundles as broken and undermine CAP-WS-05 and CAP-PORT-03. See `x-conformance-bearing` below.

type.description: REQUIRED by OKF section 11. A short string identifying the kind of concept. There is no central registry; consumers MUST tolerate unknown types. burlmd writes the constant 'Note' unless a richer type vocabulary is introduced as a product capability.

title.description: RECOMMENDED by OKF section 4.1, not required. Consumers MAY derive a title from the filename when absent. burlmd always writes it, so that a Note's display title is decoupled from its filename and therefore from its identity (ADR-004 decision 3).

description.description: RECOMMENDED by OKF. A single sentence summarizing the concept. burlmd neither writes nor requires this, but preserves it when present.

resource.description: ADVISORY, not conformance-bearing. RECOMMENDED by OKF. A URI uniquely identifying the underlying asset. Not meaningful for a personal Note, where the Note is itself the asset; preserved when present. The URI shape is documented rather than enforced -- a foreign bundle carrying a non-URI value here is still conformant.

tags.description: RECOMMENDED by OKF. Short strings for cross-cutting categorization. Preserved when present; not yet surfaced as a product capability.

timestamp.description: LEGACY (OKF v0.1). Superseded by `generated.at` in v0.2 per SPEC.md section 13.1; it is not a current v0.2 option. Listed here only so a bundle authored against v0.1 validates rather than being rejected. burlmd never writes it, and never writes `generated` either — see the `generated` property and ADR-004 decision 8 for why recording any modification time in the file would violate the Edit Fidelity constraint.

status.description: ADVISORY, not conformance-bearing. OPTIONAL lifecycle field (OKF section 5.4). Absent is equivalent to 'stable'. The values below are the ones the specification lists and the ones burlmd recognises; OKF does not close the set, so an unrecognised value is preserved and surfaced as-is, never treated as non-conformant.

stale_after.description: OPTIONAL lifecycle field (OKF section 5.5). An absolute date after which the concept should be treated as potentially outdated.

generated.description: ADVISORY, not conformance-bearing. OPTIONAL trust field (OKF section 5.2) recording how the content was produced; supersedes v0.1's `timestamp` per section 13.1. Actor identifiers follow OKF section 7: '<producer>/<version>' for tools and agents, 'human:<id>' for people, 'process:<id>' for processes. burlmd never writes this -- see ADR-004 decision 8.

verified.description: OPTIONAL trust field (OKF section 5.2). One verification event, or a list of them.

sources.description: OPTIONAL provenance field (OKF section 5.1). Materials the concept derives from.

usage_window.description: OPTIONAL provenance field (OKF section 5.1). Frames the date range that `sources[].usage_count` was measured over.

okf_version.description: OPTIONAL, and valid ONLY in the frontmatter of a bundle-root index.md (OKF section 12). burlmd does not generate index.md (ADR-004 decision 6), so a burlmd-authored bundle never declares this. Listed here so that a bundle authored elsewhere and opened by burlmd validates rather than being rejected.

verificationEvent.description: ADVISORY. A verification event; `by` is the conventional key, not an enforced one.

x-conformance-bearing.description: The only properties whose violation may set `okf_conformant = 0`. Everything else in `properties` is advisory shape documentation. An implementation that validates a whole foreign bundle against this schema and treats any failure as non-conformance is wrong.
